  marks vs 'failed check (symptom)' so break1 (input 1) and break4 (input 6)
  are distinguishable despite sharing the C1 symptom
- break4 = 23/24 (96%), traceable to input 6

Step 5: break #2 — retrieval gap (input 3)

- src/run_break2.py: turn1 retrieval sabotaged to surface a plausible coffee
  near-match (Pour-Over Dripper) while omitting the Electric Drip Maker the user
  asked for (the missing chunk)
- confident wrong recommendation follows; reads as a real production miss
- proves the subtle point: C3 (grounded) PASSES, C4 (matches need) FAILS —
  grounded in the wrong knowledge; row 3 BROKEN
- break2 = 23/24 (96%), C4 fails on turn1, traceable to input 3 alone

commit.message:
Step 2: context bundler + Context Audit table with OK/GAP/BROKEN status

- ContextBundle holds all seven inputs for a single call
- render_audit() shows one row per input with a single-word STATUS
- mark_broken(n, reason) flips exactly one row to BROKEN so a break is
  visible at a glance in one line
- empty inputs auto-render as GAP (spec gap, not missing detail)
